## Description {#details}

Assumptions are conditions that must be satisfied for a test to proceed.

Assumptions represent essential preconditions that must hold true for a test case to execute meaningfully. If an assumption fails, the test is immediately terminated, as continuing would render the results invalid or misleading.

By clearly specifying assumptions, developers can ensure that tests are only run in appropriate contexts, improving the reliability and accuracy of test outcomes. This mechanism is particularly valuable for guarding against invalid input, incomplete initialisation, or unsupported environments.

### assume() {#ga0f5febbef70eb641691b98583410a1ca}

<MemberDefinition

The <code>assume</code> function template evaluates a logical condition or custom expression and reports the result within the µTest++ framework. It is designed to provide detailed diagnostics for test failures, including the actual and expected values, when using the provided comparators (<code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#gae9dfca849300a917cb1c231d275baaa3">eq()</Link></code>, <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#ga59e4cf59954e81bc868e62b1c5c8db1f">ne()</Link></code>, <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#gac162522dcad1a6ff7c869d52d376b3ed">lt()</Link></code>, <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#ga2b5263a5b3965855aa04971bba735a56">le()</Link></code>, <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#gae2fb681444d8256f6bf827eea6b7c29e">gt()</Link></code>, <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-function-comparators/#ga34e03399670ec0b365b94b7bea788dd8">ge()</Link></code>) or custom operators.

The function template can be used with any expression that evaluates to a boolean or with custom comparators/operators derived from the local <code>detail::op</code> type. For complex checks performed outside the <code><Link to="/docs/api/groups/micro-test-plus-expectations/#ga75c3f43663a5440d78231fe572fe4a22">expect()</Link></code> logical expression (such as within <code>if</code> or <code>try</code>/<code>catch</code> statements), the result can be reported by calling <code>expect(true)</code> or <code>expect(false)</code>.

The function returns an output stream, allowing optional messages to be appended to the test report.
